---
title: "Exercise 3.1"
---

## Solution

Let $\{B_i\}$ be a pairwise disjoint sequence of sets in $\mathcal A$ and define
$$  A_i = \bigcup_{k=1}^{i} B_k.$$

Then $A_i$ is an increasing sequence of sets in $\mathcal A$ and 
$$ \bigcup_i A_i = \bigcup_i B_i.$$
Thus,
$$ \mu \left(\bigcup_i B_i \right) = \mu \left(\bigcup_i A_i \right) = \lim_{i \to \infty}\mu(A_i) = \lim_{i \to \infty} \mu \left(\bigcup_{k=1}^{i} B_k \right).$$

Since $\mu$ is finitely additive, we have
$$ \lim_{i \to \infty} \mu \left(\bigcup_{k=1}^{i} B_k \right) = \lim_{i \to \infty} \sum_{k=1}^{i} \mu(B_k) = \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \mu(B_i).$$

Hence $\mu$ is countably additive, and therefore a measure.
